title: EJS Tags
summary: Surveys the EJS tag types (output, scriptlet, unescaped output, escape, comment, include) and then has the learner complete a template that uses them with a title, a seconds value, an array, raw HTML and a footer partial.

concepts.heading: Anatomy of an EJS tag
points: Every tag opens with <% and normally closes with %>. The character right after the opening <% selects the behaviour.
Variants covered: <%= (output), <% (plain scriptlet), <%- (unescaped output), <%% (literal), <%# (comment), and <%- include(...) (insert another file).

concepts.heading: <%= value %> : escaped output
points: Contents are evaluated as JavaScript and the result is written into the page at that position, e.g. a variable holding a name.
The value is HTML-escaped, so if the string contains markup it shows up as visible text rather than being parsed.
This is the tag for anything displayed: titles, numbers, list item text.

concepts.heading: <% code %> : scriptlet, no output
points: Plain tag with no modifier runs JavaScript only; nothing is written to the page. Good for if/else, loops, variable declarations, even console.log (which prints in the server terminal, since rendering happens on the server).
Control-flow constructs can be split across several tags, with plain HTML sitting between them. The HTML between tags is emitted only when the surrounding JavaScript lets execution reach it.
Rule: every line of JavaScript needs its own opening and closing tag, including lines holding only a closing curly brace or '})'. One tag cannot wrap a region that also contains HTML elements.
Forgetting to wrap an if line in tags makes it appear as literal text on the page.

concepts.heading: <%- value %> : unescaped output
points: Writes the value as raw HTML, so 'text' sent from the server renders as bold text instead of showing the tag characters.
Swapping the minus for = shows the markup characters as plain text. The two tags differ only in escaping.
(Extra) Only use <%- with trusted content; with user input it opens the door to XSS.

concepts.heading: <%% : escape tag
points: A doubled percent in the opening (or closing) delimiter makes EJS print the delimiter as text rather than interpret it. Rarely needed, e.g. a page that documents EJS syntax.

concepts.heading: <%# comment %>
points: A hash after the opening delimiter creates an EJS comment: not executed, not rendered, and not sent to the browser (unlike an HTML comment, which still appears in page source).

concepts.heading: <%- include('file.ejs') %>
points: Pastes another EJS file at that point. Argument is the filename in parentheses; the included file must also sit in the views folder (relative paths work from the including file).
Use it for repeated pieces such as header and footer so only the changing body is written per page. Layouts and partials get a full treatment in a later lesson.
The unescaped (-) form is required so the included HTML is not escaped.

concepts.heading: Worked example: looping an array
points: Server passes an array (fruits). In the template a scriptlet tag starts a loop over it and another closes it; within each pass an li contains an output tag with the current element.
Result is an unordered list in array order.

concepts.heading: Exercise server setup
points: Starter index.js already has a route that renders index.ejs with an object containing title, seconds (from the current clock time), items (array of three fruit names), and htmlContent (a string with HTML tags).
A footer.ejs partial exists in views.
Workflow: cd into the extracted folder, npm i to install modules, run with nodemon (auto-restarts on save) and refresh the browser. Running solution.js shows the target.

code_examples.caption: Tag cheat sheet
code_examples.code:
<%= name %>            <!-- run JS, output escaped -->
<%  console.log(1) %>  <!-- run JS, no output -->
<%- html %>            <!-- output raw HTML -->
<%% literal %%>        <!-- prints the delimiters as text -->
<%# a comment %>       <!-- ignored entirely -->
<%- include('footer.ejs') %>

task.name: Complete index.ejs using the different EJS tags
task.starting_point: Extracted lesson folder with index.js (route already written and sending title, seconds, items, htmlContent), views/index.ejs with placeholders and comments, views/footer.ejs, and solution files. Run npm i first.
task.goal: Page shows the title in an h1, the current second in a paragraph, a fruit list when the second is even or 'No items to display' when it is odd, the htmlContent rendered as real HTML, and the footer pulled in via include.
steps: cd into the extracted folder, npm i, then start with nodemon index.js and open localhost:3000. Optionally run solution.js first to see the target.
Put the title variable inside the h1 with an output tag.
Put seconds in the paragraph with an output tag.

Turn the if/else commentary into real code: if (seconds % 2 === 0) show the ul, else show the 'No items to display' paragraph. Each line of JavaScript, including the closing braces, gets its own scriptlet tag; HTML stays outside tags.

Inside the ul loop over items (classic for loop with index or items.forEach((fruit) => ...)). Open the loop in one scriptlet tag, close it in another, and output each element with <%= %> inside an li. Without the output tag the literal word of the variable appears.
Render htmlContent with the unescaped tag <%- %> so the markup is interpreted. Compare what the = variant prints.
Refresh repeatedly to hit both even and odd seconds and verify both branches.
task.expected_result: Even second: heading, second count, bulleted list of apple, banana, cherry, formatted HTML text, footer. Odd second: same but with the 'No items to display' message instead of the list.

solution_code.code:
<%= title %>

Current second: <%= seconds %>

<% if (seconds % 2 === 0) { %>
    <% items.forEach((fruit) => { %>
  • <%= fruit %>
    • <% }) %>
<% } else { %>

No items to display

<% } %>

<%- htmlContent %>

<%- include("footer.ejs") %>

pitfalls: Forgetting that every JavaScript line, even a lone closing brace, needs its own tag.
Using the plain scriptlet tag where output is needed, so the loop variable never appears.
Using <%= for HTML content and seeing tags as text; or the reverse with untrusted data.
Putting footer.ejs outside the views folder so the include fails.
Reference repo diverges: its starter index.ejs holds a finished solution, htmlContent uses strong/em, and the footer carries a personal credit line to be removed.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet (section 25 has no playground file).
gaps_and_ideas: New lesson 'EJS Tags': blurb contrasting <%=, <%, <%-, <%#, <%% and include. Tasks: (1) output a variable, (2) conditional on even/odd second, (3) loop an array into li, (4) render raw HTML and observe the escaped version, (5) include a footer partial.
Starter code: route with the data object plus a template with commented placeholders.

Interactive demo idea: side-by-side editor where the learner toggles the tag type on a variable containing 'hi' and sees escaped vs raw output, plus a clock-seconds slider showing which if branch renders.
